**Unsearchable riches.** Compare Job Job 5:9; 9:10; 11:7; Rom. 11:33. The spiritual bounties of God we can see only in part, for we “see through a glass, darkly” (1 Cor. 13:12). There is a sufficiency in Christ that cannot be exhausted, for He not only possesses unsearchable riches—He Himself is the riches. And these riches are not unsearchable because they are hidden or remote, but because they are so abundant. He is rich in His grace to the Gentiles, His love to sinners, and His redeeming activity. This means that in Christ is to be found the answer to any and every human problem that can arise. His resources are inexhaustible. No wonder that Paul, with this concept and conviction, declared: “I determined not to know any thing among you, save Jesus Christ, and him crucified” (1 Cor. 2:2).

10.zh:
為要藉著教會使天上執政的、掌權的，現在得知神百般的智慧。

**藉著教會。**上帝的旨意是要教會成為祂智慧的活見證，正如康復的病人為醫師的醫術作見證一樣。與其說教會是上帝能力和智慧的媒介，倒不如說她是上帝能力和智慧的證據或證明。教會運用了全體成員的所有恩賜，就能作出最好的見證。
**天上。**見弗1:3註釋。
**執政的、掌權的。**見弗1:21註釋。救贖的廣泛宗旨，包括維護曾遭到撒但挑戰和眾天使質疑的上帝聖名和品德（參弗1:6註釋）。這是天上的生靈所關注的最偉大畫面（參林前4:9）。他們會如何看待歷史的進程呢？因為從他們的角度，可以觀察到各種勢力和事件的相互作用。
**得知。**“得以瞭解”，“可以宣佈”。
**百般的智慧。**特別是在救贖的工作上所顯示的。上帝的智慧也表現在物質世界的各樣形態，人類思維的複雜方式，以及祂接觸人類、拯救他們所用的無數方法上。只有當救贖的計劃完成以後，我們才能充分理解上帝的智慧。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第9頁；《教育論》第308頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（10–11節）**。《歷代願望》第26頁。
10.en:
**Principalities and powers.** See on ch. 1:21. The universal purpose in redemption includes the vindication of the name and character of God, which have been challenged by Satan and questioned by angels (cf. on ch. 1:6). This is the greatest spectacle that heavenly intelligences can contemplate (cf. 1 Cor. 4:9). What must the course of history look like to them, as from their vantage point they can observe the interplay of forces and events?
**In heavenly places.** See on ch. :3.
**Might be known.** Rather, “might be made known,” “might be declared.”
**By the church.** Or, “through the church,” “by means of the church.” The church was intended to be a living demonstration of God’s wisdom, even as a recovered patient is a witness to the skill of the physician. Indeed, it may be said that the church is not so much an agent of the power and wisdom of God as it is a proof or evidence of it. The church makes its witness best when it draws upon all the gifts of all its members.
**Manifold wisdom.** Especially as manifested in the work of redemption. The wisdom of God is also shown in the manifold forms in the material world, in the complexities of the human mind, and in the innumerable methods He uses to reach men and effect their salvation. The full extent of this wisdom will not be understood until the plan of salvation is ended.

11.zh:
這是照神從萬世以前，在我們主基督耶穌裡所定的旨意。

**萬世以前…的旨意。**聖經和人類的歷史都表達上帝旨意的運作。上帝創造這個世界，決不會徒然的。祂的計劃雖然在一段時期裡受到了干擾，但終必勝利完成。
**我們主基督耶穌。**見弗1:10,22,23。保羅提醒讀者，他們所承認為主的歷史上的耶穌，乃是上帝為拯救人類，彰顯祂的品德，在萬世以前所定旨意中的基督。上帝旨意要求統一，所以每一位信徒都必須完全順服他們的主。這種統一就像樂隊的指揮要求樂團中的不同樂器合奏時所作到的。教會如果不合而為一，共同獻身侍奉主，就會遭到失敗和拋棄。保羅認為：一，上帝的旨意已經向我們顯明；二，祂的旨意正在實行；三，其結果是使上帝分裂了的宇宙恢復和諧。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第397頁。
11.en:
**Eternal purpose.** Literally, “the purpose of the ages.” Scripture and life alike tell of the outworking of a divine purpose. God created the world not in vain, and although for a time His plans are hindered, they will ultimately triumph.
**Christ Jesus our Lord.** See ch. 1:10, 22, 23. Paul reminds his readers that the historic Jesus whom they acknowledged as Lord was the Christ of the eternal purpose of God to effect man’s salvation and to vindicate His character. The unity His purpose calls for requires complete submission of each believer’s will to its Lord and Master. The unity is like to that which a musical conductor expects from the different instruments of his orchestra. The church that cannot fuse into unity and a common devotion to its Lord faces certain defeat and rejection. Paul’s argument is (1) that the will of God has been revealed to us, (2) that that will is being worked out, (3) and that it will result in the restoration of harmony to God’s disrupted universe.

12.zh:
我們因信耶穌，就在他裡面放膽無懼，篤信不疑的來到神面前。

**信耶穌。**就是對祂深信不疑。我們先是憑著信心來到基督面前，然後繼續憑著信心過主所要求的生活。我們能放膽來到上帝面前，其唯一依據就是信靠我們的中保基督。只有祂能溝通自罪惡入侵以來把上帝與人類隔開的深淵（賽59:1,2）。
**放膽無懼。**parrēsia，“言論自由”（見徒4:13註釋）。
**來。**見弗2:18註釋。亞當起初能與上帝自由交往。但他後來失去了這個權利，躲在樂園的樹林中，因為他再也不能以清潔的良心坦然面對上帝了。救贖的目的，就是要幫助人類重新無拘無束地放膽來到上帝面前，不需要祭司，聖徒或禮儀之類的媒介。信徒靠著基督的功勞，可以立時到上帝面前來。
12.en:
**Boldness.** Gr. parrēsia, “freedom of speech” (see on Acts 4:13).
**Access.** See on ch. 2:18. Adam had that free intercourse with God at first, but, having lost it, he hid himself among the trees of the garden, because he could no longer face God with frankness and a clear conscience. The effect of redemption is to restore to man a new and bold access to God without fear or restriction, and without the need of any intermediaries such as priests or saints, or ritual. God is immediately accessible to the trusting soul, through the merits of Christ.
**The faith of him.** Meaning, doubtless, our faith in Him. We come to Christ in the first instance by faith, and we continue, by faith, to live the life that is called for. We can come to God with boldness only on the basis that we have faith in Christ as our mediator. He has been the only One to bridge the gulf that has separated man from God since the entrance of sin (Isa. 59:1, 2).

13.zh:
所以，我求你們不要因我為你們所受的患難喪膽，這原是你們的榮耀。

**所以。**由於外邦人現在是基督身體的一部分，上帝萬世以前的旨意正被實現，我們可以自由地來到上帝面前，由於這種偉大奇蹟的發生，保羅對讀者提出了一個微妙的請求；叫他們不要為他因帶給他們福音的福惠所受的患難而灰心。
**喪膽。**egkakeō.“疲乏”，“灰心”。保羅的意思既可以是“我求（上帝）使我不喪膽……”，也可以是“我求（你們）不要喪膽”。後者更符合上下文和保羅的風格。被囚的使徒非常希望他的羊群不至因他的遭遇而灰心。他所擔心的不是自己，而是他們。他們可能會以為，他所傳的道理沒有什麼拯救的能力，保羅所信靠的上帝不關心祂僕人的命運，他們自己也可能很快面臨這樣的試煉了，而他們確實會面臨這樣的試煉。這是使徒牽掛他信仰之子女的感人例子。保羅非常清楚，患難對於經歷者和旁觀者都是一種考驗。如果經歷者和旁觀者都能勇敢地忍受患難，從中獲益，他們就會加倍地得到榮耀。
**你們的榮耀。**保羅像一個好牧人，把自己和羊群視為一體。他既能在自己的患難中得榮耀，他們也必與祂分享榮耀。他遭受患難，是因為擔任上帝使徒和使者的崇高職分。以弗所教會是他擔任使徒職分的果實。因此他們應該反映這榮耀。當基督身體的一部分受苦時，整個身體一同受苦。
**懷愛倫註釋（13–21節）**。《懷愛倫傳略》第439頁；《餘民教會》71頁。
13.en:
**Wherefore.** Because the Gentiles now belong to the body of Christ, because the eternal purpose is being fulfilled, because we have free access to God, and because such great and marvelous things have occurred, Paul makes a delicate request of his readers; namely, that they be not too much distressed over his sufferings that have come on account of his bringing to them the blessings of the gospel.
**Faint.** Gr. egkakeō, “to grow tired,” “to become discouraged.” Paul may mean, “I ask [God] that I may not faint …,” or “I ask [you] not to faint.” The latter sense fits the context and Paul’s general style better. The apostle in prison was anxious that his flock be not disturbed by his plight. He was concerned, not so much for his own sake, but for theirs. They might conclude that what he had preached had little saving power in it; that the God in whom Paul trusted was unmindful of His servant’s fate; that they themselves might soon face similar trials, as indeed they would. This is a touching instance of the apostle’s solicitude for his children in the faith. Paul well knew that tribulation is a test for those who look upon it as well as for those who undergo it. Suffering courageously borne is doubly glorious when both onlookers and sufferers draw virtue from it.
**Your glory.** Paul, like a good pastor, identifies himself with his flock. If he finds glory in his tribulation, they will share it with him. He is suffering on account of his exalted office as apostle and ambassador of God, and the Ephesians are the fruit of that apostleship. Hence they are entitled to reflect the glory. When one part of the body of Christ is in pain, the whole body suffers in sympathy.

14.zh:
因此，我在父面前屈膝，

**因此。**見第1節註釋。經過一段插話之後，本節繼續第一節所中斷的思路。
**屈膝。**關於屈膝作為祈禱的姿勢，見路22:41；徒7:60；20:36；羅14:11；腓2:10
有文本在“父”前面有“我們的主耶穌基督的”。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《傳道良助》第178頁；《先知與君王》第48頁；《成聖的人生》第84頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–15節）**。《使徒行述》第11頁；《歷代願望》第25頁；《證言》卷六第366頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–19節）**。《服務真詮》第426頁；《證言》卷八第289頁；《證言》卷九第183頁。
14.en:
**For this cause.** See on v. 1. The thought that was interrupted in the first verse is here resumed, following an extended parenthesis.
**Bow my knees.** For kneeling as a posture in prayer see Luke 22:41; Acts 7:60; 20:36; 21:5; Rom. 14:11; Phil. 2:10.
**Of our Lord Jesus Christ.** Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 10) the omission of this phrase.

15.zh:
（天上地上的各（或作：全）家，都是從他得名。）

**全家。**或“各家”。原文兩種譯法都可以，但按本句的結構，通常譯為“各”，而不是“全”。當然也有譯為“全”的例外（太3:15；28:18；徒1:21等）。弗2:21的譯法比較獨特，譯為“全房”或“各房”。而在弗3：15中則譯為“全家”或“各家”。由於這裡的原文沒有明確的界定，故必須根據上下文來確定譯文。保羅講的似乎是合一的問題，認為天上的生靈和地上的聖徒同屬一個大家庭。如果譯成“各家”，就必暗示天上的好幾個家庭。聖經裡並沒有這樣的說法。因此譯成“全家”似乎較好，表達了眾生之父上帝之家的統一性和完整性。這是使徒經常論述的主題。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《教育論》第306頁；《善惡之爭》第677頁；見創1：26懷愛倫註釋。
15.en: **The whole family.** There has been much discussion as to whether this phrase should be translated, “the whole family,” or “every family.” The Greek may be rendered either way, although normally a construction such as appears here would be translated “every” and not “the whole.” However, a number of exceptions may be cited in which a construction such as is used here clearly stands for “the whole,” or “the entire” (Matt. 3:15; 28:18; Acts 1:21; etc.). A notable exception is Eph. 2:21, where the same construction is rendered “all the building,” or “the whole structure” (RSV), whereas in ch. 3:15 the RSV reads “every family.” Since the Greek here is not clearly definitive, the context must decide as to the translation to be adopted. Paul appears to be speaking of unity and seems to conceive of the beings in heaven and the saints on the earth as one large family. If the translation “every family” is adopted, it seems necessary to conceive of several families in heaven. Such the Scriptures do not describe. It seems better therefore to adopt the reading “the whole family,” which conveys the sense of unity and wholeness of the community of God, the Father of all, a theme to which the apostle frequently reverts.

16.zh:
求他按著他豐盛的榮耀，藉著他的靈，叫你們心裡的力量剛強起來，

**豐盛的榮耀。**參弗1:18。指上帝賜福與人的程度。所以上帝的子民享有無限的資源。人所依仗的，只是自己的軟弱和卑微；上帝則依仗祂無限的豐盛與榮耀。保羅不滿意他的信徒只作名義上的基督徒。他要他們領受豐富的恩典，追求更深更高的屬靈生命，分享上帝國度的豐盛榮耀。
**心裡的。**原文暗示有能力進入並留在心中。一個人的屬靈生命的能力不是源於他的本性。他自己拿不出什麼東西來，也沒有任何值得誇口的。
**力量剛強起來。**剛強的力量就是上帝的能力，藉著聖靈的運行而賜下。只要基督徒不斷成長，使他悔改的能力必繼續運行在他們心中。許多基督徒就在這一點上失敗了。他們沒有認識到屬靈的成長也和他們悔改時一樣，需要上帝的恩典。正如體力依賴食物，智力依賴思維，維持屬靈的生命需要聖靈的直接同在和大能。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第200頁；《傳道良助》第262頁；《證言》卷八第132頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（16–19節）**。《健康勉言》第593頁；《善惡之爭》第476頁；《成聖的人生》第84頁；《證言》卷二第522頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（16–21節）**。《基督教育原理》第180頁。
16.en:
**Riches of his glory.** Compare ch. 1:18. This is the standard by which God bestows His blessings upon mankind, hence the limitless resources available to the child of God. Man measures by his own weakness and insignificance; God by His unlimited riches and glory. Paul is not satisfied that his converts should become merely nominal Christians. He wants them to receive abundantly of the graces, to plumb the depths and scale the heights of spiritual life, to partake of the glorious riches of the kingdom of God.
**Strengthened with might.** The might that strengthens is the power of God. The power is conveyed through the operation of the Holy Spirit. The same power that converts men must continue in them if there is to be Christian growth. Here is where many Christians fail. They do not recognize that spiritual endurance requires as much of the grace of God as did the initial conversion. As the physical strength is increased by food and the intellectual life by thought, so the spiritual life is sustained by the immediate presence and power of the Holy Spirit.
**In the inner man.** The Greek suggests power entering into and remaining there. The vital spiritual powers within a man have not sprung from his own nature; he has nothing of his own to offer, nothing of his own of which to boast.

18.zh:
能以和眾聖徒一同明白基督的愛是何等長闊高深，

**能以。**所要掌握的主題不是一般的理解力可以領會的。所以保羅祈求能讓聽眾獲得一種特別的理解力。
**眾聖徒。**見弗1:1註釋。有些屬靈的工作是在個人心中進行的；但有些事情是上帝的教會所共有的，例如對基督之愛的理解。這種共同的認識把信徒聯合在一起。
**明白。**直譯為“抓住”；喻指“理解”。
**闊。**保羅沒有說明這裡所用的是什麼尺度。解經家們有各種解釋。最簡單的解釋也許是保羅中斷語句，彷彿為他所思考的題目所震撼。當他默想那奧秘，就是基督住在我們裡面，上帝的愛，和基督身體的合一時，（弗3:19），心中深受感動。正如我們在群星璀璨的夜晚從各個方位觀察上帝無限的宇宙時，會不勝驚訝一樣。
**懷愛倫註釋（18–19節）**。《使徒行述》第469頁；《基督比喻實訓》第129頁；《歷代願望》第670頁；《基督教育原理》第178頁；《福山寶訓》第34，76頁；《證言》卷二第213，266頁；《證言》卷五第264，740頁；《證言》卷七第214頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（18–20節）**。《證言》卷八第335頁。
18.en:
**May be able.** The subject to be grasped is beyond ordinary comprehension; therefore Paul prays that his hearers may receive a special enabling power for the attainment of it.
**To comprehend.** Literally, “to seize”; metaphorically, “to perceive.”
**All saints.** See on ch. 1:1. There are certain spiritual transactions that take place only in the individual heart, but there are other matters that belong to the community of God, and this comprehension of the love of Christ is one of them. It is the common possession that binds believers together.
**Breadth.** Paul does not state to what the dimensions mentioned in this clause apply. Commentators have given various interpretations. Perhaps the simplest explanation is that Paul breaks off his sentence as though overwhelmed by the magnitude of the subject he is contemplating. He is simply yet profoundly moved, as he contemplates the mystery—the indwelling Christ, the love of God, the unity of the body of Christ, or specifically the love of Christ (v. 19). It is as though on some starry night the spectator looks out on God’s unbounded universe in all directions, lost in wonder.

19.zh:
並知道這愛是過於人所能測度的，便叫神一切所充滿的，充滿了你們。

**這愛。**顯然不是指我們對基督的愛，而是祂對我們的愛。
**過於人所能測度的。**基督的愛過於人所能測度的，因為它無窮無盡，白白賜下，永不枯竭，不斷展示新的見地。這是我們愛的經驗增長的泉源（約壹4:19）。人類僅僅用指尖接觸到充分體驗基督之愛時所獲得的生命大能。
**上帝一切所充滿的。**見弗1:23註釋。這是基督住在生命中所結出的光榮成果。教會就像一個器皿，要讓屬天的恩惠滿溢，使基督身體的每一個肢體都展示或反映“上帝的豐盛”。保羅正在就人的本性及其恩典中成長的可能性，闡述一個十分高明的見解。人是照上帝的形象所造的，賦有發展的潛力和與“上帝的性情”（彼後1:4）有份的崇高特權。上帝施恩並不小氣。這些恩惠引導人不斷加深對上帝旨意的理解，用屬靈的能力充滿人生命的空虛之處。上帝的豐盛實際上是居住在基督裡面的（西2:9），所以上帝的“豐盛”就藉著基督住在人心中（見弗3:17）而臨到人類。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第308頁；《先祖與先知》第64頁；《證言》卷二第215頁；《證言》卷三第467頁；《證言》卷五第105頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（19–20節）**。《傳道良助》第262頁。
19.en:
**Love of Christ.** Here, are apparently, not our love for Christ, but His love for us.
**Which passeth knowledge.** Christ’s love is beyond the knowledge of human kind because it is infinite and free, never exhausted, and ever presenting new fields of understanding. It is the fountain of our own growing experience of love (1 John 4:19). Men have but touched with their finger tips the power for living to be found in experiencing fully the love of Christ.
**Fulness of God.** See on ch. 1:23. This is the glorious consummation to the work of the indwelling Christ in the life. The church, like a vessel, is to be filled to the brim with heavenly grace, so that the individual members composing the body of Christ exhibit or reflect something of the “fulness of God.” Paul is presenting a most exalted view of the nature of man and of his possibilities for growth in grace. Man was made in the image of God. He was given images of God. He was given capabilities of development and the high privilege of becoming a partaker of the “divine nature” (2 Peter 1:4). The blessings of God are not parceled out parsimoniously. They lead to an ever-increasing comprehension of the mind of God, to a filling up of the void and empty places in men’s lives with spiritual power. Since it is Christ in whom God’s fullness is actually found (Col. 2:9), the divine “fulness” comes to man by the indwelling of Christ in the heart (see Eph. 3:17).

21.zh:
但願他在教會中，並在基督耶穌裡，得著榮耀，直到世世代代，永永遠遠。阿們！

**榮耀。**因為恩典拯救的工作，惟有把稱頌，讚美和榮耀都歸給上帝。教會或信徒都沒有任何功勞或榮耀。
**在教會中，並在基督耶穌裡。**讚美上帝的原因就在這兩個地方：在教會里，因為教會是反映祂榮耀的地方；在基督裡，因為祂是教會這個身體的元首。
**直到世世代代，永永遠遠。**就是永世無窮。
**阿們。**見太5:18註釋。
使徒的祈禱和《以弗所書》的第一部分就此結束了。在上帝對祂犯有錯誤但仍有希望的子民所發的應許中，包含著奇異的榮耀和奧秘。這個主題是人的言語所難以表達的。它鼓舞我們的心，潔淨我們的靈，給我們帶來上帝的國完全降臨的活潑盼望。
21.en:
**Glory.** Literally, “the glory.” To God alone belongs the credit, recognition, and honor for the saving work of grace. There is no place for the assumption of virtue and glory on the part of the church or its members.
**In the church by Christ Jesus.** Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 10) the reading “in the church and in Jesus Christ.” The reasons, then, for praising God are found in these two places: in the church, because there His glory is reflected; in Christ, because He is the head of the body, the church.
**Throughout … end.** Literally, “unto all the generations of the age of the ages,” that is, to all eternity.
**Amen.** See on Matt. 5:18.
So ends the apostle’s prayer and the first part of the epistle. Amazing glory and majesty embodied in the promises of God to His erring yet hopeful ones has been the theme, beyond human language to express. It leaves the heart uplifted, the spirit chastened, and gives a living hope for the coming of the kingdom of God in its fullness.

0.zh:
**一、卷名**
早期教會幾乎一致認為這封信是寫給以弗所教會的，每一份已知的文本都毫無例外地冠以《以弗所書》的卷名。然而在兩種最古老最有權威的文本，即西奈抄本和梵蒂岡抄本，還有更早一些的紙莎草抄本即46號切斯特比提抄本中，第一章第一節均無“在以弗所”四字。四世紀的巴西勒說他見過古代的抄本里省略了“以弗所”。奧利金和德爾圖良所作的陳述也支持這個看法。所以第二世紀的有些抄本顯然略去了這幾個有疑問的字。
值得注意的是，雖然保羅在以弗所度過三年時期，工作取得了成果，無疑也結交了許多密友，信中卻沒有個人的問候，而是論述適合於所有教會的教義問題。
對於這一點，一般有三種答案：
１、這封信是寫給老底嘉教會的。（見西4:16）
２、這封信是給所有亞細亞的教會傳閱的。
３、這封信是寫給以弗所教會的。
把第二種說法和第三種說法結合起來，似乎構成了一個比較滿意的答案。這封信很可能是寫給亞細亞行省的都市以弗所教會的，意在讓該地區各教會傳閱。這就解釋了認為這封信是寫給以弗所教會的傳統說法，也解釋了為什麼有些古代抄本沒有“在以弗所”幾個字。原件可能有好幾份抄本在附近教會中傳閱。不論怎樣，這封信已被以弗所的信徒，也許還有亞細亞行省中其他教會的信徒所閱讀。
**二、作者**
《以弗所書》為保羅所著，這一點一直沒有受到疑問。直到上個世紀，許多現代解經家才得出結論說這封信不是保羅所寫，或者說保羅只是寫了其中的一部分。他們說《以弗所書》只是重複了《歌羅西書》的內容，其中有些用語透露出作者從未去過以弗所（弗3:2,3；弗4:21）。他們指出信中沒有向教會信徒的問候語，而保羅實際上在那裡已工作了三年（徒20:31）。他們說這封信的風格，情感和宗旨都與保羅不符，甚至說在監獄裡的人不可能寫出語氣如此歡快的信來。關於這些問題的討論，見本註釋卷五181-183頁。
從早期把正典和偽經及外傳區別開來的時候起，《以弗所書》一直是列在新約正典之中的。這封書信正典地位的外證是十分充分的。羅馬的克萊門特顯然瞭解它（公90年），第二世紀的伊綱爵和波利卡普也證實了這封書信。穆拉托里經目和後來的伊裡奈烏（185年），亞歷山大的克萊門特（190-195年），德爾圖良（207年）以及其他早期的作者，都提到《以弗所書》為保羅所著。本註釋亦採取保羅為作者的觀點。
**三、歷史背景**
保羅行使了羅馬公民的權利上訴於凱撒，故就被押往羅馬，約於公元61年春天到達。他在這裡被監禁了兩年，所以這封信可能寫於公元62年左右。
他雖然身為囚犯，卻顯然享受某些自由（參弗6:19；西4:3-11），有機會進行思考和寫作。他利用了這個機會給亞細亞的教會發出了許多教義上和實際行為方面的指示。這封信寫作的時間似乎與《歌羅西書》和《腓利門書》同時，因為《以弗所書》和《歌羅西書》是讓推基古帶的，《腓利門書》是讓他的同伴阿尼西母帶的（弗6:21；西4:7-9；門12；參《使徒行述》456頁）。《以弗所書》是四封監獄書信中的第一封，而這段時期中所寫的《腓立比書》可能是四封中的最後一封。有人說《以弗所書》可能是保羅被關在凱撒利亞期間寫的，但是在羅馬寫信的證據要充足得多。書信是他在被囚時寫的，這一點沒有什麼疑問（弗3:1；弗4:1），然而羅馬監禁的條件似乎更有利於寫信（徒28:16,20），他在羅馬被監禁時希望很快獲得自由（門22），而他在凱撒利亞則沒有這種願望表露出來。保羅久已盼望訪問羅馬（羅15:23,24），到了羅馬他又打算去歌羅西，而在凱撒利亞，他從來沒有去歌羅西的意圖。
保羅寫這封書信的時間和環境構成了他信息的背景。嗜血成性的尼祿當時在位。他放蕩、奢侈而又兇殘。例如據歷史記載，羅馬元老院的議員皮達皇斯•塞肯得斯被一名奴隸殺死以後，作為報復，就有400名左右的奴隸被處死。大約在保羅寫《以弗所書》的那一年（公元62年），在不列顛島爆發了布狄卡起義，據說在羅馬方面就有“七萬多”人連同成千上萬的起義者被處死。在這種很亂的形勢下，經過思考和聖靈的感動，保羅發表了他最高尚的言論之一，敘述了那唯一能恢復人類和平和團結的信仰。這封信在保羅寫給教會的九封信中被稱為“新約的阿爾卑斯山”。
**四、主題**
《以弗所書》的主題就是在基督裡的合一。他所致信的教會里有猶太人和外邦人，有亞洲人和歐洲人，有奴隸和自由民──代表著這個四分五裂的世界中各種各樣的人，他們都要在基督裡恢復到團結統一。這就要求個人、家庭、教會和整個人類的統一性。在每一位信徒的生活上恢復了統一性就保證了上帝整個宇宙的統一性。在整封書信中合一的主題是含蓄的，而不是明言的。
使徒以高尚的屬靈語氣宣佈了他的主題，呼籲所有的人要有最好的品格和行為，不僅在教義和組織上達到統一，而且在元首基督裡，在基督奇妙的身體──教會之中達到合一。“在基督裡”乃是關鍵的詞語，可是很難找出最關鍵的一節來。因為書信中沒有一節不是以某種形式表現了基本的主題的。揀選，赦免，預定，家庭關係──一切都是在“基督裡”。
使徒在這封信中恩典要比信心談得多，在他的早期著作裡，他強調的是個人與得救的關係。在這封信裡他則強調團體、教會和身體。他講述了“在基督裡”，而不是“藉著基督”所成就的；講到基督住在信徒裡面，而不是基督被釘十字架。
保羅並不是以一種正式辯論或陳述的形式來展開他的主題的。他只是把他所得到的啟示說出來，不是因為他有什麼特別的聰明和眼光，而只是因為他是上帝施恩的器皿，得以看見主的國度屬靈的團結的重要性而已。
也許可以說，《以弗所書》對今日的教會所起的作用，就像《加拉太書》和《羅馬書》對十六世紀和宗教改革運動所起的作用一樣。關於個人與家庭的關係，家庭與民族的關係，所有的人與教會和上帝的關係，基督教應當說什麼呢？保羅回答說，基督乃是萬物的中心和終結，藉著教會實行祂的旨意，“使天上地下一切所有的，都在基督裡面同歸於一”（弗1:10）。
今日最大的需要就是那種保障個人自由的統一，不強求一致的統一。保羅所領受的啟示為縈繞於所有善良之人心頭的問題提供了唯一的答案。

**1. Title.** The early church was in almost universal agreement that this epistle was addressed to the church at Ephesus, and every known manuscript, without exception, bears the title “to the Ephesians.” However, the words en Ephesō, “at Ephesus,” in ch. 1:1 are lacking in Codex Vaticanus and in Codex Sinaiticus, two of the most ancient and authoritative manuscripts, as well as in the Chester Beatty MS P, a still earlier papyrus manuscript. Basil, of the 4th century, says (Against Eunomius ii. 19) that he had seen ancient manuscripts in which en Ephesō was omitted. Statements by Origen (Commentary) and Tertullian (Against Marcion v. 17) support this idea. It is clear, therefore, that there were some manuscripts of the 2d century in which the words in question were omitted. See Vol. V, pp. 181–183.
It is also significant that although Paul had spent three years in Ephesus in fruitful ministry, and no doubt had made many intimate friends, there are no personal greetings or salutations in this epistle. Rather, it deals with doctrines applicable to the universal church.
There are three solutions commonly offered for this problem:
a. The letter was addressed to the church at Laodicea (see Col. 4:16). b. It was an encyclical to the churches in Asia. c. It was addressed to the Ephesians.
A combination of the second and third theories appears to satisfy the question. It may well be that the letter was sent to the church at Ephesus, the metropolis of the proconsulate of Asia, with the intention that it should be sent also to other churches in the area. This would account for the tradition that the church at Ephesus was addressed in the epistle, and also for the fact that very early there were extant copies of the book which did not contain the words en Ephesō, and which may have been copies of the original autograph that circulated among the neighboring churches. In any case, this letter doubtless was read by the believers in Ephesus, and probably by others also in the province of Asia.
**2. Authorship.** The Pauline authorship of Ephesians was never questioned until the last century, when many modern critical scholars arrived at the conclusion that it was not Pauline, or at least that it was only partially so. It was suggested that it was only a wordy repetition of Colossians, and that certain expressions indicate that the writer never was in Ephesus (Eph. 3:2, 3; 4:21). It was pointed out that there are no salutations to the members of the church at Ephesus, where Paul had labored for some three years (Acts 20:31). It was declared that the epistle is not Pauline in style, sentiment, or aim, and it was even proposed that no man in prison could write such a cheerful letter. For a discussion of these problems see Vol. V, pp. 181–183.
From the earliest times, when forgeries and apocryphal books were being separated from the genuine, the Epistle to the Ephesians was placed in the New Testament canon. The external evidence for its right to that status is overwhelming. It was known apparently to Clement of Rome (c. .. 90), and was also attested by Ignatius and Polycarp at the beginning of the 2d century. Paul is mentioned by name as the author in the Muratorian Fragment and later by Irenaeus. (c. .. 185), Clement of Alexandria (c. .. 190–195), Tertullian (c. .. 207), and many other early writers. This commentary proceeds from the point of view that Paul was the author.
**3. Historical setting.** Having exercised his rights as a Roman citizen and appealed to Caesar, Paul was sent to Rome, where he probably arrived in the spring of .. 61. Here he was a prisoner for two years. Thus it is likely that this epistle was written about .. 62.
As a prisoner he apparently enjoyed certain liberties (cf. Eph. 6:19; Col. 4:3–11), which afforded him opportunity for reflection and writing. He took advantage of this to send to the churches in Asia much doctrinal and practical instruction. This letter would appear to have been written about the same time as Colossians and Philemon, for Tychicus was the bearer of Ephesians and Colossians, and a traveling companion of Onesimus, the bearer of Philemon (Eph. 6:21; Col. 4:7–9; Philemon 12; cf. AA 456). Ephesians, then, would be one of the four letters of the first imprisonment, Philippians also having been written during this period, probably the last of the four (see pp. 105, 106).
It has been suggested that Ephesians may have been written during the apostle’s imprisonment in Caesarea, but the evidence for Rome is much stronger. That he was in prison at the time of writing there can be no doubt (chs. 3:1; 4:1), but the conditions of his confinement in Rome seem to have been more favorable to the writing of his letters (Acts 28:16, 20). While in the Roman prison he hoped for speedy liberation (Philemon 22), whereas there is no indication that he cherished any such hope while in Caesarea. Paul had long wished to visit Rome (Rom. 15:23, 24), and when there he planned to go to Colossae (Philemon 22). However, he never seems to have had the intention of going to Colossae from Caesarea.
Paul wrote this epistle in times and surroundings that well form a background to his message. The bloody Nero was emperor; licentiousness, luxury, and murder were rampant. It is recorded, for example, that when L. Pedanius Secundus, a senator of Rome, had been murdered by a slave, in accordance with legal rights some 400 slaves of his household were condemned to death in retribution. About the year of the writing of the epistle (.. 62), the revolt of Boadicea, or Boudicca, took place in Britain, when, it is said, “over 70,000” on the Roman side perished, along with many thousands of the rebels. In the midst of such confusion, and as a result of deep thought and inspiration, the apostle produced one of his noblest utterances concerning the faith that alone could restore to man peace and unity. It has been called “the Alps of the New Testament,” and stands in the midst of peaks—Paul’s nine epistles written to seven churches.
**4. Theme.** The subject of Ephesians is unity in Christ. He was writing to a church (or churches) consisting of Jews and Gentiles, Asiatics and Europeans, slaves and freemen— all symbols of a disrupted world that was to be restored to unity in Christ. This would necessitate unity of person, family, church, and race. The restoration of individual unity in the life of each believer assures the unity of God’s universe. The theme of unity is implicit, where it is not explicit, throughout the book.
The apostle announces his theme in a tone of high spiritual exaltation, and urges upon all the highest character and conduct, for the purpose of unity not only in doctrine and organization but in Christ the head, and in the church, the mystical body of Christ. Although “in Christ” is the key phrase, it is difficult to select a key verse, for there is scarcely a verse that does not present in one form or another the basic theme. Election, forgiveness, predestination, home relationships—all are “in Christ.”
The apostle has less to say about faith than about grace. In his earlier writings he stressed the relation of the individual to salvation; here he stresses the group, the church, the body, and he speaks of being “in Christ” rather than of things accomplished “through Christ”; of Christ living in the believer rather than of Christ crucified.
Paul does not develop his theme as a formal argument or proposition. He speaks simply of what came to him by revelation, not because of any superior intellect or insight, but because he was an instrument of God’s grace to whom had been granted a vision of the essential spiritual unity of the kingdom.
It may be asserted that what the books of Galatians and Romans were to the 16th century and the Protestant Reformation, Ephesians is to the church of today. What does Christianity have to say regarding the relations of the individual to the family, of the family to the nation, of the nation to the race, and of all to the church and to God? Paul answers by presenting Christ as the center and end of all things, working out His purposes through the church, gathering “together in one all things in Christ” (ch. 1:10).
There is no more urgent need today than that of a unity that preserves the freedom of the individual, unity without rigid uniformity. The apostle was granted a revelation that offers the only solution to a problem that haunts the minds of all good men.

An exhortation to purity of life, 5:1–14. 4. Foolishness and wisdom, 5:15–21. C. Duties of home relationships, 5:22 to 6:9. 1. Husband and wife, 5:22–33. 2. Children and parents, 6:1–4. 3.
